summary: systemd_service controls systemd units (services, timers, etc.); systemd remains an alias. name is required with state/enabled/masked, globs aren't supported, and actions run enable, mask, then state.
questions: What module manages systemd services in Ansible?
Can I pass a glob to systemd_service?
What order are systemd_service changes applied?

answer_card.title: Manage systemd units with systemd_service
answer_card.answer_md:
`ansible.builtin.systemd_service` manages systemd units (services, timers, ...). `ansible.builtin.systemd` is an alias.
- `state`/`enabled`/`masked` require `name`; no globs.
- Order: enable/disable → mask/unmask → state.
